title: Introduce tonal-layering, compact typography, and micro-radius/shadow system for dense data surfaces
text:
Introduce tonal-layering, compact typography, and micro-radius/shadow system for dense data surfaces

description:
Summary:
This ticket captures the work to introduce a tonal-layered color palette, a micro-scale typography ramp for compact data surfaces (tables, dense charts, compact list views), and a small-radius/expressive shadow (elevation) system tuned for high-density interfaces. Goal is to improve legibility at small sizes, increase semantic clarity in cramped UIs (tables, row states, overlays), and reduce visual noise while preserving contrast and accessibility across themes.

Scope:
- Define a tonal-layered color system (base/foreground/muted/overlay/interactive) that can be composed into semantic lanes (primary, neutral, success, caution, critical) with 3–4 tonal steps each. Include both light and dark theme mappings and guidance for token derivation.
- Create a micro typography ramp: 10px, 11px, 12px, 13px with defined line-height and relative weights for labels, metadata, table bodies, and compact button/text controls. Document truncation rules, minimum tap targets for interactive micro elements, and scaling guidance for accessibility.
- Introduce a micro-radius scale (0, 4, 6) specifically for dense surfaces and a complementary small-elevation/shadow ramp with subtle diffuse shadows intended to separate rows/overlays without making surfaces feel lifted.
- Update tokens JSON (semantic tokens and alias tokens) and example token usage for Table, CompactCard, MiniButton, SparklineChart, and Dense List components.
- Provide migration guidance and codemods for Frontend to consume updated tokens (tokens rename map, deprecation notices).

Acceptance criteria:
- Token definitions (color, type, radius, elevation) live in the design tokens repo and include token names, hex/RGBA/alpha steps, line-height, weights, and usage notes.
- Design kit (Figma) updated with components using the new tokens; previews for default/dark and high-contrast.
- Accessibility checks: AA contrast for primary/foreground pairs at micro sizes where possible; documented exceptions and compensations (e.g., bold weight or increased tracking).
- Engineering integration: tokens exported in the pipeline, validated by the token CI, and a Frontend PR that switches Table and CompactCard to the new tokens behind a feature flag.
- Rollout plan: gated canary rollout for 10% of sessions for 2 weeks with visual diff snapshots to catch regressions (visual QA + automatic diffing).

Trade-offs and decisions pending:
- Contrast vs. density: micro typography at 10–11px benefits density but may fail AA for some color combinations. Decision: default to 11px for body micro copy for AA; reserve 10px for non-critical metadata where product requires max density and provide opt-in classes.
- Shadow expressiveness: stronger shadows improve separation but increase perceived depth and may conflict with flat aesthetic. Proposal: keep shadows extremely subtle (low Y-offset, high blur, low alpha) and rely on tonal layering for most separation.

Implementation notes / links:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Token+Modernization+PRD
- Figma kit (tokens + component previews): https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/Redwood-Design-Tokens
- Tokens repo (draft branch): https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-tokens/trees/feature/tonal-layering
- Frontend integration PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/frontend/pull/7842

Migration and rollout steps:
1) Finalize and merge token definitions to main in design-tokens repo.
2) Publish token package and update token CDN/tag.
3) Open Frontend PR that wires Table and CompactCard to new tokens under feature flag.
4) QA: visual diff snapshots + manual checks across breakpoints and high-contrast mode.
5) Canary rollout at 10% -> 50% -> full after 2 weeks each stage and sign-offs.
6) Deprecate old token aliases in next minor with deprecation table and codemods.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: micro typography fails contrast for some locales with longer glyphs. Mitigation: run locale visual QA, increase weight where necessary, document locale-specific fallbacks.
- Risk: front-end layout shifts due to line-height changes. Mitigation: provide strict line-height/metrics and a migration checklist for components with snapshots.

Stakeholders and reviewers:
- Product: Marco Liu (product lead for Console)
- Engineering: Priya Desai (Frontend lead), Omar Haddad (Platform tokens)
- Accessibility: Maya Chen

Notes: This ticket is intentionally narrow (dense-surface token work) and will be accompanied by separate tickets for full-system scale token rebaseline and component refactors for larger controls.

comments:
2026-02-21 Sofia Martinez: Initial kickoff meeting held with Eng and PM. Agreed to prioritize Table and CompactCard for first wave. Action: design to deliver token draft by 2026-02-28.
2026-02-28 Aisha Patel: Draft tokens uploaded to feature branch in design-tokens. Shared Figma frames for 10/11/12/13px micro type with examples in tables and sparklines. Noted several color pairs failing AA at 10px.
2026-03-03 Priya Desai (comment): Frontend prototype toggles tokens via feature flag. Observed layout jitter in CompactCard due to line-height change — proposed adding utility classes to opt-in. Will open PR for review.
2026-03-05 Maya Chen (accessibility): Ran automated contrast checks and manual sampling. Recommendation: bump micro body to 11px/semibold for primary rows; allow 10px for secondary metadata only with documented exceptions.
2026-03-06 Marco Liu (product): OK to proceed with 11px default. Please include rollout schedule and canary dashboards in the PR description.
